_note: Literature in English, Form 1 Learner's Book.
_unitThree: The manuscript never titled its third unit: it types a bare 'UNIT THREE' as the heading and lists it that way in its own hand-typed contents, while units one and two carry their subject ('UNIT ONE: INTRODUCTION TO LITERATURE', 'UNIT TWO - ORAL LITERATURE'). So the contents page showed one untitled unit among three, and the running header on every page of the unit said only 'UNIT THREE'. The subject is not in doubt - the unit opens on written literature and runs through prose, drama and poetry - so give it the same NAME: SUBJECT shape its siblings use. This is the manuscript's own gap, not an engine fault, which is why it is fixed here and not in src/typeset/.
//manuscript-correction: APPLIED DIRECTLY TO THE .docx, and it must be re-applied if that file is ever re-converted from the original. The manuscript bolds every activity label but two - 'Activity 1: In groups, attempt the following riddles?' and 'ACTIVITY: 4 Composing Short Stories' were typed as ordinary body text - so the engine, which starts a callout box on a bold or heading-styled label, did not box them: the riddles label printed as a loose line above its table, and Activity 4 was swallowed into Activity 3's box together with its own four questions. Both runs now carry <w:b/><w:bCs/>, which is all the other 62 labels in the book have. This cannot be done with an override: the box is built at IMPORT time, before overrides run, and the only override that reaches it (boxifyLoose, via boxActivities) rebuilt just one of the two and as a framedsection rather than the exercise box its siblings use. It must not be fixed in src/typeset/ either: a scan of every manuscript in books-to-typeset shows that dropping the bold requirement engine-wide would turn the sentence 'Key points include:' into a Key Points box in Geography For Teachers and newly boxify up to 111 paragraphs in Home Ecnomics Grade 4 TG. A copy of the file as it was is kept beside it as 'LIT in ENG F1 LB.docx.bak-before-bold'. The author should bold both labels in the next issue.
//plot-diagram: Printed page 109's plot diagram (media image19.jpg) was REDRAWN, not upscaled. The manuscript's own bitmap is a screenshot of a third-party graphic: a tiled 'ELEMENTS OF FICTION' watermark runs diagonally across the header about eight times and cuts through the PLOT title, and seven opaque grey rectangles sit on top of the artwork obscuring words in all six definition boxes - Conflict, Exposition, Climax, Rising Action, Falling Action and Resolution. It is greyscale and soft. Upscaling it (which had already been done, to 1625px / 308 DPI) only sharpened the watermark and the grey blocks. Because this is Freytag's pyramid - the diagram Unit Three teaches from, and which the pages after it build on - the page could not be taught from as it stood. The replacement is drawn in TYPST, and its source is kept beside it as 'LIT in ENG F1 LB-art/plot-diagram.typ' so it can be corrected rather than redrawn. It carries the same six element names and the same six definitions, transcribed from the legible parts of the original. No third-party artwork is involved, so there is no licensing question. It is drawn at the width it is PLACED at in the book (134mm, the B5 text column), which is the point of it: an earlier node-canvas attempt was drawn oversized and scaled down, which landed its annotations near 6pt on the page. Rendered at 400 DPI, 2111px across, well over the 300 DPI floor. Nothing here is engine work: it is one book's bad source picture.
